proposal.description_long: An August 2016 report by The Times described a Ukrainian prosecutor’s memo about Paul Manafort’s earlier work in Crimea. The prosecutor alleged that Manafort organized anti-NATO and anti-Kyiv protests there in 2006 on behalf of Viktor Yanukovych’s Party of Regions. The Times reported that the protests led to cancellation of planned NATO exercises and quoted the memo as saying Manafort viewed autonomy as a way to bolster Yanukovych’s party among local voters. The Times said the memo set out legal options for prosecuting him but no charges were pursued after Crimea’s 2014 annexation, citing a lack of evidence. At the time of the article, Manafort was Donald Trump’s campaign chief. The story documents the existence of the allegation and the reported status of the inquiry, not a proven finding. It does not establish that Manafort caused the cancellation, aided Russia’s later annexation, or participated in Russia’s 2014 seizure of the peninsula. The 2006 alleged protests and the 2014 annexation remain distinct events.
proposal.description_medium: In 2016, The Times reported that a Ukrainian prosecutor's memo alleged Paul Manafort organized anti-NATO and anti-Kyiv protests in Crimea in 2006 for Viktor Yanukovych's Party of Regions. The report said planned NATO exercises were canceled and that charges were not pursued for lack of evidence after Crimea's annexation. The allegation does not establish that Manafort helped Russia annex Crimea.
proposal.description_short: A Ukrainian prosecutor reportedly accused Manafort of organizing anti-NATO protests in Crimea in 2006.
proposal.title: Ukrainian Prosecutor Alleged Manafort Organized 2006 Crimea Protests
